root_cause.text: __sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup() in the SCTP input path failed to validate that the full variable-length ASCONF address parameter fit within the chunk before passing it to from_addr_param(), causing out-of-bounds/uninitialized reads on truncated parameters.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states the function “only checks that the ASCONF chunk can hold the ADDIP header and a parameter header” and then calls from_addr_param() “which reads the full address ... trusting the parameter's declared length,” and the patch adds `if (sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length) > ntohs(ch->length)) return NULL;` to ensure the whole parameter lies within the chunk.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states the function “only checks that the ASCONF chunk can hold the ADDIP header and a parameter header” and then calls from_addr_param() “which reads the full address ... trusting the parameter's declared length,” and the patch adds `if (sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length) > ntohs(ch->length)) return NULL;` to ensure the whole parameter lies within the chunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length bounds check for ASCONF address parameters to reject truncated chunks before address parsing reads past the chunk.
intent_record.what: A new bounds check was added in __sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup() after locating the ASCONF address parameter: it compares sizeof(*asconf) plus ntohs(param->p.length) against ntohs(ch->length), and returns NULL if the parameter would extend past the containing chunk. A comment was also added explaining that this prevents af->from_addr_param() from reading a variable-length address from a truncated trailing ASCONF chunk.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now rejects ASCONF chunks whose embedded address parameter length exceeds the chunk length, preventing subsequent parsing code from reading beyond the valid data and using uninitialized bytes when handling truncated packets.

grouping_result.intent: Add a length bounds check for ASCONF address parameters to reject truncated chunks before address parsing reads past the chunk.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds the missing bounds validation for variable-length ASCONF address parameters before parsing, which is exactly the root cause of the out-of-bounds/uninitialized read on truncated chunks.

candidates.rationale: This computes the address-parameter pointer immediately after the ASCONF header without first verifying that a complete variable-length address parameter is present within the chunk, enabling later parsing to read past truncated input.

This dereferences the unvalidated address parameter to read its type before confirming the full parameter fits in the received chunk, which can trigger out-of-bounds or uninitialized reads on truncated ASCONF parameters.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement dereferences the ASCONF address parameter via param->p.type before verifying that the full variable-length parameter is contained within the chunk. On a truncated ASCONF parameter, this can read beyond the received data or consume uninitialized memory, matching the root cause.

This computes the pointer to the variable-length ASCONF address parameter immediately after the ASCONF header without any bounds validation that such a parameter fully exists in the chunk. It sets up the later unsafe dereference and parsing that cause the vulnerability.

It computes `param = (union sctp_addr_param *)(asconf + 1);` and then immediately dereferences it via `param->v4.param_hdr.type` and passes it to `af->from_addr_param(&paddr, param, peer_port, 0);` without validating that the full variable-length ASCONF address parameter is present within the chunk. Although `__sctp_rcv_walk_lookup()` checks the enclosing chunk bounds with `ch_end = ((__u8 *)ch) + WORD_ROUND(ntohs(ch->length)); if (ch_end > skb_tail_pointer(skb)) break;`, that only ensures the chunk itself is within the skb, not that the internal address parameter is complete/trustworthy. There is no validation of the parameter length field or of `param` against `ch_end` inside `__sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup()`. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.
